describes.method: internal first-order administrative polygons, drawn as de facto boundaries according to who controls the territory (Natural Earth); simplified here once with Douglas-Peucker at 0.01 degrees and coordinates rounded to four decimals
describes.resolution: Natural Earth 1:10m scale, further simplified to a 0.01 degree tolerance (about 1.1 km) in this build
describes.completeness: Natural Earth calls it the toughest dataset to keep current as countries rearrange their units, states the statistical codes (FIPS, ISO, HASC) are incomplete, and labels the theme still in beta

describes.extent: every earthquake of M7 or larger that the USGS ComCat lists in the window (137 earthquakes, counted 2026-10-13)
describes.method: the forecast of js/aftershock-core.js, unchanged and with nothing fitted, issued 1 day after each mainshock from the aftershocks recorded by then, and compared with what the catalogue holds for the windows that followed; scored by reliability (mean forecast probability against the fraction of sequences with one) and by coverage of the forecast 95 percent range
describes.completeness: the set is chosen by a rule, not by hand, and nothing is dropped for having gone badly; only magnitudes at or above the catalogue completeness count in the scores

(2012) global seismotectonic regionalization (15 regimes)

describes.completeness: every one of the 3601 x 7201 grid points is covered by a regime, and the decoded runs reproduce the upstream count for each of the 15 regimes, or nothing is written

describes.extent: 1,229 first-level unit rows covering 1,096 ISO 3166-2 units in 51 countries; the earliest row starts in 1927 and open-ended rows run to the present (measured on the bundle)
describes.method: Reconstruction, not a survey: today's Natural Earth 10m admin-1 outline of a unit that still stands, drawn only over the span on which three records agree it may be (Wikidata states when the unit began and, if it did, ended; the country's own stated inception is a floor; the ground lay inside one polity of the era record; no OpenHistoricalMap-derived unit already speaks for that ground), and only for a country whose every unit may be drawn on those dates. Dates and names are Wikidata's, joined by ISO 3166-2 code, never by spelling; an undated unit is not carried back
describes.resolution: unit outline simplified once at 0.01 degrees with four decimals; spans exact between the dates on which a test can change, to the day
describes.completeness: A unit absent here is not a statement that it did not exist: units that fail any test are withheld for that span, and a country is drawn only where all its units pass, so countries are either whole or silent (the bundle lists the units it deferred and refused)

describes.extent: 3,608 first-level unit rows from 134 reconstruction dossiers; the earliest row starts in 1727 and the latest ends in 2020 (measured on the bundle)
describes.method: Reconstruction by IntMap, not a surveyed record: a unit on a span is a union of finer atoms (Natural Earth admin-1, RISTAT 1897 uyezds, geoBoundaries, Japanese N03 1920 and e-Stat 2020 areas, Amasyali kazas) whose boundaries are the historical lines, and every membership is a stated fact with a citation in a dossier; nothing is drawn by hand, smoothed or interpolated. A span is drawn only if the ground lay in one polity of the era map on that date, and it yields to OpenHistoricalMap and to every publisher's dated record
describes.resolution: the precision of each atom set as its publisher released it, simplified to a 0.004 degree tolerance with four decimals for the overview; spans are dated to the day, with exclusive ends
describes.completeness: Only units whose membership could be established from cited facts on atoms that carry the historical line; a line no atom carries is not drawn and is listed as unresolved in the dossier, and a span withheld by a test is reported with its reason, so absence here is not a statement that the unit did not exist

describes.extent: 127 first-level unit rows from five publishers (Roman provinces 28, Canada 9, Palestine and Syria-Lebanon 6, Russian Empire 1897 45, Republican China 39); the earliest row starts in 117 and the latest ends in 1950 (measured on the bundle)
describes.method: Each publisher's own survey of first-level units, with the publisher's dates and their stated precision carried beside every row (a year-precision date is never printed as a day); identical consecutive snapshot rows are collapsed into one span; nothing is interpolated; every row yields to OpenHistoricalMap wherever an in-force OpenHistoricalMap unit already covers a quarter of its ground
describes.resolution: unit outlines simplified to a 0.004 degree tolerance with four decimals; dates as the publisher gave them, with exclusive ends
describes.completeness: Only the regions and eras these five publishers surveyed, and only where OpenHistoricalMap holds no unit; a region absent here is not a statement that it had no first-level units

describes.resolution: unit outlines simplified to a 0.004 degree tolerance with four decimals; dates as the publisher gave them, with exclusive ends
describes.completeness: Only the regions and eras these two publishers surveyed, and only where OpenHistoricalMap holds no unit; absence is not a statement that a region had no first-level units

describes.resolution: unit outline at 0.004 degree tolerance with four decimals; dates to the day where OpenHistoricalMap states a day, otherwise to the month or year

describes.extent: 6,474 settlements in 125 country codes with 9,241 dated name spans; by source 611 handwritten, 2,809 Wikidata, 808 Pleiades, 2,246 OpenHistoricalMap (measured on the bundle)
describes.method: A date-bounded name is attached to a settlement by name and place together, never by spelling alone: a tile label is renamed only if its own spelling is one of the row's and it lies within the row's guard radius, which is half the distance to the nearest other settlement answering to one of the row's spellings (GeoNames cities500 evidence), capped and floored. Spans and names are those of the upstreams (OpenHistoricalMap, Pleiades, Wikidata) and of the handwritten record; nothing is interpolated
describes.resolution: one point per settlement; each name span has signed YYYYMMDD endpoints with a per-endpoint precision (day, month, year, a period boundary from a vocabulary, or open)

describes.method: One representative point per place, as Pleiades computes it: usually a centroid of the geometries of all the place's published locations, the same coordinates as the location when there is a single point, and possibly a point that matches no single location when the place has lines, polygons or conflicting locations
describes.resolution: one representative point per place; each dated name carries a start and an end year taken from Pleiades (approximate-source-period, as the bundle marks it)
describes.completeness: A selection of Pleiades, not the gazetteer: places under CC BY 3.0 (not share-alike) typed settlement, with a representative point and at least one dated name that ends before the snapshot year; places the hist-cities bundle already ships are left out
describes.accuracy: Pleiades states no formal accuracy figure for representative points and warns that large Barrington Atlas bounding-box polygons (about 0.5 to 1.0 degrees) can put the point very far from the actual site

describes.extent: 1,738 cities worldwide, each a single central point; 10,352 dated population figures (measured on the bundle)
describes.method: Population of cities as the two books state it, not re-estimated here and not interpolated. Chandler (2250 BC to AD 1975): "an urban area including suburbs lying outside of the municipal area, and omitting farmland lying within the municipality", suburbs outside the municipal area counted as urban population only from after 1962; each figure is a demographic factor for the city, and early ones use the city's spatial extent with a common population density. Modelski ancient and classical (3700 BC to AD 1000): archaeological site assessments and population-density factors. Modelski AD 2000: UN 2000 Demographic Yearbook data for "cities proper" governed as one unit, agglomeration figures only where no other data were available. The paper notes that gaps between values in the source tables can be hundreds or thousands of years, and calls the values in them measured or interpolated (this bundle adds no interpolation)
describes.resolution: city point (one central latitude and longitude per city) x the table year a figure is stated for; irregular years, not a regular grid
describes.completeness: A city is listed only above a size threshold: Chandler over 20,000 inhabitants from AD 800 to 1850 (over 40,000 for Asian cities) and over 40,000 after 1850; Modelski 10,000 or more (3500 to 1000 BC), 100,000 or more (1000 BC to AD 1000), 1,000,000 or more (AD 2000). Absence means not listed, not did not exist. Per the paper, over 600 of the 1,741 original cities have only one population value
describes.accuracy: The paper provides no statistical analysis of error and did not correct or validate the population estimates; Modelski marks figures of questionable reliability in his tables. Locations carry the geocoders' certainty rank: 1 (confirmed by three geocoding sources), 2, or 3 (least accurate); the paper reports 75% of cities at rank 1, 13% at rank 2 and 12% at rank 3

describes.extent: 19,345 spellings (the keys scripts/histcities/*.mjs join on), each listing every cities500 settlement that answers to it (measured on the bundle)
describes.method: For each spelling the record joins on, every GeoNames cities500 settlement whose name, asciiname or untagged alternatename matches it exactly, with no population sort, no deduplication, no stop-word or length filter; each hit keeps the country, longitude and latitude in decimal degrees (WGS84, as GeoNames states), population and feature code
describes.resolution: settlement point (longitude, latitude) per hit
describes.completeness: Only settlements in GeoNames cities500, which the readme defines as all cities with a population over 500 or seats of administrative divisions down to PPLA4, and only for the spellings the record uses; a place GeoNames lacks is absent here

describes.extent: Wikidata labels in nine languages for 1,244 items named by QID, 185 CShapes, 773 era-snapshot and 32 era-base English names, plus 100 translated descriptions (measured on the bundle)
describes.method: Three lanes: a polity whose record states a Wikidata QID is asked for that item directly; an English name with no identifier is matched to the Wikidata item carrying that string, scored against where and when the map draws the shape, and a tie is refused so the name is left out; prose descriptions written by the era cartographer (aourednik/historical-basemaps) are translated by IntMap and marked as translations, not as names any source attests. Labels are Wikidata's own, never interpolated
describes.resolution: one label per language per Wikidata item or English name string
describes.completeness: Only names a lane could resolve: a name Wikidata does not carry, or whose match was tied, has no row, so absence is not a statement that no name exists; each row carries a bitmask of the languages a source actually wrote

describes.accuracy: Natural Earth states its coastline accuracy is questionable for northern Russia and southern Chile

describes.method: route counts: distinct airline routes between airports (existence only, no frequency, seats or passengers; the supplier states routes are directional and a carrier appears once per route even if codeshare), resolved to country pairs; volumes: ST.INT.ARVL, international inbound tourists (overnight visitors), total visitors where tourist counts are unavailable, each trip counted as a new arrival, collection methods varying by country (World Bank indicator note, source UN Tourism)

describes.method: Wikidata SPARQL query over P31/P279* of Q1739545; one record per facility with status, units and net MW where the item states them (IAEA PRIS is not read: no machine-readable route)

describes.completeness: the class held 930 items when measured on 2026-09-09; records with no label or no usable P625 coordinate are dropped, so 638 are shipped

describes.extent: the global ocean on the upstream 0.25 degree grid (cell centres -89.875 to 89.875 N, -179.875 to 179.875 E); land cells carry no velocity
describes.method: a climatological mean of 28 geostrophic-current fields from satellite altimetry spread evenly across the period, plus an Ekman surface current from 24 blended wind-stress fields (Ralph and Niiler 1999); named paths are integrated through the mean field
describes.resolution: 0.25 degree (about 28 km) for the annual field; 0.5 degree for the twelve monthly climatologies

describes.extent: world: polities drawn by CShapes 2.0 and the war record, with 101 dated Wikidata events; 940 day-precision entries on 315 calendar days (1886-12-30 to 2014-03-18) and events dated 1346 to 2024 (measured over the committed bundle)
describes.method: a border day is read off the map's own records: a polity in force on the day but not the day before appears, the reverse ends, and one in both whose drawn area differs by at least 1 km2 is redrawn; the OpenHistoricalMap record, record seams, names the record does not date and the sheets before 1689 are left out and counted in `skipped`
describes.resolution: day
describes.completeness: states only what a record states on the day the record states it: 1 January CShapes rows are kept but marked maybeYearOnly, and the omissions are counted in `skipped` (1 seam, 881 not a day record, 21 undated name, 97 unchanged)

describes.extent: 17,438 diplomatic features worldwide, 445 distinct country codes (11,339 embassy, 5,355 consulate, 744 other)
describes.method: Overpass query of nwr["amenity"="embassy"] and nwr["office"="diplomatic"], run in 60-degree longitude slices because a global union times out
describes.resolution: one point per OSM node, way or relation (the coordinate of a node, otherwise the centre Overpass returns)

describes.extent: 14,965 features worldwide (36 spaceport, 200 launch pad, 3,108 radio telescope, 11,621 satellite ground station)
describes.method: Overpass query of nwr tags aeroway=spaceport, man_made=launch_pad, military=launchpad, man_made=satellite_dish, man_made=telescope with telescope:type=radio, and communication:satellite, run in 60-degree longitude slices
describes.resolution: one point per OSM node, way or relation (the coordinate of a node, otherwise the centre Overpass returns)

describes.extent: 9 bodies: Sun, Mercury, Venus, Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune; the Earth is not in the set
describes.method: one 2k texture per body downloaded and shipped byte for byte, with no re-encoding by this build
describes.resolution: 2048 x 1024 pixels per body, equirectangular, -180..180 by 90..-90

describes.extent: 5 bodies: Mercury (599 features), Venus (700), the Moon (700), Mars (700) and Pluto (73)
describes.method: IAU-approved feature names read from the gazetteer results table, each with its centre latitude and longitude, diameter in km and feature type; only the 700 largest features per body (by diameter) are kept
describes.completeness: the largest features only, at most 700 per body (the Moon alone has over nine thousand named features)

period.note: the catalogue's own `year` field of the streamed dataset of each unit (46 / 1 / 52 / 85 / 100 / 157 units for 2020 / 2021 / 2022 / 2023 / 2024 / 2025), measured; it is the year of the dataset, not a survey date

describes.extent: 441 city or ward units in 45 prefectures of Japan, measured on the committed registry; union of the tileset root regions 127.63E 20.42N to 153.99E 43.19N; a unit appears only if the catalogue lists building 3D Tiles for it
describes.resolution: building models at LOD2 (293 units) or LOD1 (148 units), all textured, as the catalogue's lod and texture fields state; the best variant at LOD2 or below is chosen per unit

period.note: the 336-hour model window from 2011-03-11T05:46Z; the deposition values are decay-compensated to 2012-06-28 (the paper that uses the file says so, the IRSN file does not)

describes.extent: the area around Fukushima Daiichi, longitude 138.13 to 141.78 and latitude 35.17 to 39.57 (measured on the 1,740 survey cells)
describes.method: measured Cs-137 ground deposition (mean of the MEXT/NRA aerial radiation monitoring in each cell, compiled by IRSN) compared with the js/radiation-model.js plume model as shipped (nine members: 3 seeds x 6/10/20 PBq, ERA5 wind); nothing is fitted to the survey
describes.resolution: survey cells of 0.05 degree (1,740 cells, 1.72 million aerial measurements); the model deposits on a 0.01 degree grid

describes.extent: parties designated by three authorities (OFAC SDN, UK Sanctions List, EU FSF) linked to 192 countries; 432 authority x country links, 32246 designated parties in all
describes.method: count of parties the list of each authority designates, per authority and country, by kind, regime and measure; a country is the address country the list states, else nationality (flag for a ship); a party with addresses in several countries is counted in each
describes.resolution: authority x country

describes.extent: the hosts the reader's browser asks (scripts/outbound-hosts.json) and the services the elections layer is rebuilt from, plus the production Atlas evaluation and reader field-speed
describes.method: one nightly probe per host with the verdict alive, refused, dead or unobserved, kept as one character per host per measured night; a half that could not be read is null with the reason, never an older answer
describes.resolution: one verdict per host per night

describes.extent: all active global subduction zones as published by USGS (27 regional models in this bundle)
describes.method: three-dimensional slab-surface geometry (depth, strike and dip grids) per subduction zone (Hayes et al. 2018)
describes.resolution: 0.05 degree sampling in longitude and latitude, as published; shipped without decimation
describes.completeness: each regional model is valid only inside its clipping-mask polygon; the release states that outside it the models should not be used

describes.extent: all active global subduction zones as published by USGS (27 regional models in this bundle)

describes.extent: 1,150 bodies: asteroids of 150 km and larger, trans-Neptunian objects brighter than H 5.5, every numbered comet, potentially hazardous asteroids brighter than H 18, plus an editorial list of spacecraft targets and famous bodies
describes.method: osculating heliocentric orbital elements (J2000 ecliptic) at the epoch each body states, propagated two-body from that epoch: mean anomaly from the time of perihelion where SBDB gives one, otherwise from ma at epoch, and from q and tp on the hyperbolic branch for e of 1 or more
describes.completeness: a selection by size, brightness and editorial pick, not the whole catalogue
describes.accuracy: osculating elements drift from the real orbit as planets perturb it (and, for an active comet, non-gravitational jetting): adequate to show where a body is in the solar system, not to point a telescope (the bundle's own warning)

describes.extent: 17 spacecraft (Voyager 1 and 2, Pioneer 10 and 11, New Horizons, Parker Solar Probe, Solar Orbiter, Juno, JUICE, Europa Clipper, Lucy, Psyche, BepiColombo, Hayabusa2, OSIRIS-APEx, JWST, Gaia), each over its own span within 2000-01-01 to 2045-01-01 (measured over the committed bundle)
describes.method: heliocentric J2000-ecliptic position (AU) and velocity (AU/day) per sample, Julian Date TDB, from Horizons; the sampling step is per spacecraft (3 to 120 days) and the client interpolates between samples with a cubic Hermite
describes.resolution: a sample every 3 to 120 days per spacecraft, set by how fast the body turns in the heliocentric frame
describes.accuracy: trajectories, not telemetry: for spacecraft with no contact (Pioneer 10 and 11) the position is propagated from the last fix, and the bundle marks each craft active, lost or ended

describes.extent: all-sky; 98,887 stars with V magnitude from -1.44 to 9.5 (measured over the committed bundle, read from Hipparcos)
describes.method: right ascension and declination in degrees at J2000.0, V magnitude, B-V colour index and parallax in mas per star; stars with no astrometric solution are dropped, and a parallax of 0 means no usable parallax (non-positive, or below 2 sigma)
describes.completeness: stars at or brighter than V 9.5 (the builder's magnitude limit for the Hipparcos catalogue); 78,963 carry a usable parallax and 19,924 do not (measured over the committed bundle)

describes.extent: 702 submarine cables and 1,922 landing points worldwide, planned cables included (96 flagged isPlanned)
describes.method: cable inventory, metadata, landing points and connection topology from the TeleGeography submarine cable map; route geometry is NOT the TeleGeography schematic line but a surveyed position (NOAA, EMODnet, ACMA) where matched to a cable by name and place, otherwise a least-cost path between real anchors
describes.resolution: routes reconstructed over a 1/12 degree sea-floor grid; surveyed pieces simplified to within 40 m
describes.accuracy: per-cable quality is measured, not asserted: 22 verified (published surveyed position), 675 reconstructed (least-cost path), 5 estimated (geodesic where the router found no path)

describes.extent: the whole Earth (1440 x 720 equirectangular cells of 0.25 degree), derived from the global PB2002 plate-boundary model

describes.resolution: 0.25 degree (about 28 km at the equator) for the raster; the underlying PB2002 steps are about 30 km apart

describes.extent: the CelesTrak `active` group of Earth-orbiting objects, worldwide; the other groups listed in groups.json are membership lists only
describes.method: GP mean elements (Brouwer mean elements for the SGP4 propagator, fitted to US Space Surveillance Network observations, as CelesTrak states), 3-line TLE sets each with its own epoch; propagating them with SGP4 loses accuracy as the epoch recedes

describes.extent: 51 U.S. state-level units (50 states and the District of Columbia)
describes.resolution: 1:110m (Natural Earth admin-1 generalisation)

describes.extent: all 60 U.S. presidential elections, 1789-2024, each with its state-by-state electoral vote; the national popular-vote share is recorded for 51 of them (none for 1789-1820)
describes.method: Electoral College result per state (the candidate who received the electors of each state), with electoral votes per candidate and national popular-vote share where one was recorded; the state fill is by electoral votes because that is the one basis that exists for every election
describes.resolution: state x election

describes.method: a catalogue of Holocene volcanoes and their eruptions compiled by the Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program, revised as eruptions are reported and as the literature is reviewed

describes.resolution: 0.05 degrees (7200 x 3600 cells; 3600 x 1800 at 0.1 degrees for phones) from terrain pixels spaced about 1223 m at the equator
describes.completeness: measured on the committed manifest: 7,371,340 cells (28.44%) carry a land value

period.note: measured: earliest start and latest end over the 6 wars in the bundle

describes.extent: worldwide: the USGS query carries no area limit, and EONET events are listed with or without a placed position
describes.method: a digest per closed ISO week (Monday 00:00 UTC to Monday 00:00 UTC): USGS earthquakes of magnitude 5.5 or more and NASA EONET natural events, each kept with the originating source EONET names
describes.resolution: one ISO week; each event with its own USGS or EONET time and position
describes.completeness: not every event: earthquakes below magnitude 5.5 and wildfires with a stated burned area below 10,000 ha are left out (wildfires left out are counted per week); an event EONET gives only as a polygon is listed but not placed; a week fetched less than 7 days after it ended is provisional and asked again

describes.extent: global; 3,205 Disease Outbreak News items, placed by ISO 3166 alpha-3 country code where WHO names a country (160 codes; 180 items name no single country and carry none); no coordinates
describes.method: a Disease Outbreak News item is published by WHO, under Article 11.4 of the International Health Regulations (2005), for an event of unknown cause with potential international concern, a known cause shown able to cause serious harm and spread internationally, or high public concern; the country is joined through the taxonomy of WHO itself
describes.resolution: one record per published notice; country level
describes.completeness: not exhaustive: WHO states that Disease Outbreak News is not an exhaustive list of the events WHO is responding to globally

describes.extent: global; all 1,273 properties on the World Heritage List (991 cultural, 240 natural, 42 mixed) in 173 States Parties, with 6,009 component-part points
describes.method: the List as UNESCO publishes it, one point per component part of a serial or transboundary property; the in-danger flag is taken from Wikidata statements with no end date, not from the unmaintained danger column of the UNESCO feed
describes.resolution: one point per component part of a property
describes.completeness: the whole List: the bundle holds every one of the 1,273 properties UNESCO states
describes.accuracy: the bundle flags 52 sites as in danger (Wikidata, built 2026-09-09) while the UNESCO List page, read 2026-11-20, states 58 properties In Danger; the two counts are not reconciled

describes.extent: DESA states 233 countries and areas; the bundle carries 9,345 destination-origin pairs over 231 destinations and 233 origins, at eight dates (1990, 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020, 2024)
describes.method: UN estimates of the stock of international migrants by destination and origin; in the 2024 edition 60 countries and areas received a full reassessment from new census or register information, and the remaining estimates extrapolate those published in the 2020 edition
describes.resolution: country or area of destination x country or area of origin x year

describes.extent: the hosts IntMap's browser code can contact, one row per host (191 in the committed file), each with what it is sent and the Privacy section 4 words that say so
describes.method: derived from scripts/outbound-hosts.json by deriveConnectionLedger, with the protocol each host is contacted over and the socket the code opens there, read from the browser code

describes.extent: 236 river-basin outlines, each carrying a name only
847 ecoregion polygons, each carrying its ecoregion name, biome name and display colour
global grid, equirectangular, -180..180 by 90..-90
describes.method: mean annual precipitation (CHELSA V2.1 bio12), a 1981-2010 climatology, encoded in the PNG as log-scaled millimetres
describes.resolution: 0.1 degree (3600 x 1800 cells)

describes.extent: land cells of a global grid (cells with no gauge analysis, sea and the poles, are 0), equirectangular, -180..180 by 90..-90; one band of 360 rows per year
describes.method: GPCC Full Data Monthly Product Version 2022 gauge analysis, the twelve monthly totals of each year summed into an annual total per cell
describes.resolution: 0.5 degree (720 x 360 cells), one value per cell per year

describes.extent: every name IntMap's browser code writes to localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB or Cache Storage (106 in the committed file), found in js/, src/, sw.js and the inline scripts of every tracked page; cookies are not a storage area here
describes.method: every localStorage and sessionStorage setItem, indexedDB.open and caches.open call is parsed with acorn and its first argument resolved through the file's own bindings (parts no binding fixes become *), then each name is joined to its row in scripts/device-storage-words.json

describes.extent: the 18 sampled years from 500 BC to 2019, on a 0.25 degree grid of the land the historical map draws
describes.method: per sampled year, the share of each polity's land carrying a first-level unit, the polity and unit land measured, the polities with none, partial and full coverage, the number of rows drawn from a date no upstream stated, and the first-level double claims by kind (seam, duplicate, contested)
describes.resolution: 0.25 degree grid cells

describes.extent: the 18 sampled years from 500 BC to 2019, on a 0.25 degree grid of the land the historical map draws
describes.method: per sampled year and polity, the percentage of its land carrying a first-level unit and the cells left uncovered, each uncovered stretch labelled with its present-day country and a reason
describes.resolution: 0.25 degree grid cells

describes.method: pairs of first-level units drawn over the same ground at the same instant, each with its overlap interval and its kind (seam, duplicate, contested; contested pairs are not judged)

describes.extent: the hosts whose row in scripts/outbound-hosts.json carries an offline statement (4 in the committed file, 3 allowing a saved copy and 1 not); a host whose row says nothing is absent
describes.method: derived from the offline statement of each host row (allowed, kind, pathPrefix, basis, why) by deriveOfflineSources; no supplier terms are read at build time

describes.extent: 4 GIBS raster products (MODIS Terra NDVI 8-day, GHRSST MUR sea ice concentration, GHRSST MUR SST anomalies, AMSR-U2 soil moisture), each with its own first and last served date (measured over the committed bundle)
describes.method: the first and last served date of each product, found by bisection on real tile requests: GIBS answers 404 outside a layer's temporal extent and 200 inside it; an 8-day layer is also probed on an off-period day
describes.resolution: daily for three products, 8 days for the MODIS NDVI composite (its period start days only)
